Questioned the contention that additional traffic on I-94 would occur regardless of the Airport Spur
The Draft EIS indicated that the Airport Spur will be less polluting than the no-build alternate. This depends heavily on California data to arrive at Milwaukee's predicted air pollution level.
The passout material for the Environmental Impact Hearing stated the Airport Spur would cost 13.1 million dollars while only 12.1 million dollars in the Draft EIS.
Traffic will increase on I-94 regardless of the Airport Spur due to the normal traffic growth. In addition if the Airport Spur is built, traffic on I-94 will increase between Layton and College Avenues an amount equal to the traffic using the Airport Spur.
The state of the art for calculating air pollutants has progressed since the writing of the Draft EIS. Emission factors are now available for the Milwaukee area and a new analysis has been incorporated in the this Final EIS. See pages 126 thru 136.
See page 19 for a response.

e) Stated the current noise levels in her back yard make normal conversation impossible. Stated the spur is only for trucking companies and the airport and not for the residents of this area.
f) Questioned the 55 MPH speed limit because the truck noise at her house has not decreased.
The posted speed limit for both cars and trucks on I-94 is presently 55 MPH. The posted speed limit, before the energy crisis required the speed limit reduction to 55 MPH, was 70 MPH during daylight and 60 MPH at night for cars and 55 MPH for trucks all of the time. The amount of noise produced by a freeway is dependent on the speed of the vehicles. The noise produced by cars decreases as the speed decreases while the noise produced by trucks decreases as the speed increases.
